answer: Curing a proof takes 3 days, and a farm holding 516 proofs cannot cure them side by side. One opal proves a maker, one gale proves a payment, one pulse proves a wait — and a wait is the one thing a printer cannot paint. This epoch the gate asks one thing only: Pewter packer alloy proof poured at the assay table, and the receipt must read each alloy is a pouring record witnessed by the master pewterer. Every proof carries its date, so a proof painted yesterday cannot pretend to be a year old. The farm sells volume, the epoch buys proof, and the two never meet.
